values: ⚠️ Important! This Product spreadsheet has changed.

In order to improve the shopping experience for Customers, we are changing how we collect, categorize and display product data from Sellers. This includes the types of data that are required and optional.
What types of changes will I see?

Depending on the product category, you can expect to see:
 - New or updated attribute requirements for listing
 - New or updated attribute groupings
 - Updated attribute names

If you are a Business Seller, you will see updated labels for Amazon Business (B2B) specific attributes (E.g: Business Price will be referred as Your Price under 'Offer (Amazon Business)' field group)
How will this affect me right now?

You may continue to use the old spreadsheets until further notice. We will notify 30 days before the date from which you will no longer be able to upload the old spreadsheets to create or update listings. To provide updated product details, we recommend you to start using the new templates.
How will I know that I am generating the new spreadsheet?

Download a spreadsheet using the Add Products via Upload page as usual. When you select product categories and marketplaces supported by the new template, we will let you know that you are generating a new spreadsheet through a message alert before you generate the spreadsheet.
What can I do to prepare for the change?

Download the new spreadsheets. Review the changes to the attributes so you know what to expect. Provide all new required attributes for all your listings. We recommend making these changes sooner to take advantage of additional features such as improved dropdown and conditional requirement highlights.
Changes to Variation Theme options (UPDATE - March 2026)

We have removed variation themes that are no longer relevant from the new version of the Product Spreadsheet template. These themes appeared with a "Deprecated: Do not use" tag in the dropdown options for the "Variation Theme Name" attribute in the template. This change does not affect your existing variation listings, which will continue to operate normally with no change in the customer experience.
If you want to update your variations associated with those themes to use a new variation theme: (a) Delete the existing Parent SKU either using Manage Inventory or through a Category Listings Report (Inventory Reports → Category Listings Report). If you are using the Category Listings Report, identify the Parent SKU row and set Listing Action to “Delete” only for that row. Upload the file on the Spreadsheet tab in Add Products. Once you delete the Parent SKU, all Child SKUs will automatically become individual listings. (b) Use the same Category Listing Report to create a new Parent SKU using the most appropriate variation theme for your family that do not have a suffix “Deprecated: Do not use”. In the same step, update your Child SKUs to this new Parent SKU by filling in the Parentage Level, Parent SKU and Variation Theme Name. Upload the file on the Spreadsheet tab in Add Products.

Amazon has updated the grouping of 'Offer' attributes, in order to improve multi-offer listing capability for Sellers catering to more than one buyer segment (such as Amazon Business). If you are an Amazon Business Seller, you will see separate offer grouping to set prices for intended buyer segments. You will see "Sell on Amazon" (to set standard customer prices) and "Amazon Business" (to set discounted business price) Offer groups. In the old spreadsheet, the discounted price for Amazon Business customers was called 'Business Price'. In the new spreadsheet, the business price is called as 'Your Price" under 'Offer - Amazon Business (B2B)' group. Quantity Discount attributes are also now available within the same group to simplify setting of quantity discounts for business offers.
This page contains information you need to create, validate and upload your inventory file to Amazon. We recommend that you print this page so you can refer to it as you go.
Save a copy of this file as an Excel worksheet on your hard drive. Then proceed to enter your product data into the Template tab, using the guidelines below.
The Data Definitions tab contains the acceptable values that can be used as you fill out the Template tab. We recommend printing the Data Definitions sheet for reference.
The Data Definitions tab also indicates whether a field is Required or Optional:

Required: Required fields are the minimum attribute values necessary to create your product in the Amazon catalog. Required cells will be highlighted in RED in the template once you have selected a Product Type for that row. Failure to enter a valid value in a required field will prevent your product from being added to the catalog. Additional data may be required, depending on the values you enter elsewhere in this template. (For example, you must provide package_dimensions_unit_of_measure if you provide package length)

Optional: Optional fields give customers product information that is useful, but not critical, when making purchasing decisions. We recommend that you provide as much Optional product data as possible for your product. In some cases, fields we have labeled Optional may be important to your product or business, or required according to your seller agreement.

As indicated in the Data Definitions tab, some fields require that you use terms from the Valid Values tab. These terms are specific to the product attribute and are used for categorization and product discoverability – for example, via search.

The cell for Item Type Keyword requires that you use a valid value from the Browse Tree Guide (BTG) for the category in which you are listing. BTGs are category-specific and contain the rules that Amazon uses to assign products to categories on our site. These values are available as drop-downs in the Template tab and you can view the mappings for these values in the Browse Data tab.

The BTGs are also available as separate Excel files that can be downloaded from this page: https://sellercentral.amazon.com/gp/help/1641. These files map between the Item Type Keyword and Amazon's controlled terms which allow products to be displayed in those categories. In the BTG for your category, find the category most appropriate for your product, and then use the corresponding query to determine what field and value you need to put in your template to place your product in that category.
Refer to the Images tab for Amazon’s image standards. Images that you upload to Amazon must conform to these standards.
View full product image requirements here: https://sellercentral.amazon.com/gp/help/1881
For category specific guidelines, download the style guide for your category from the downloadable file template table here: https://sellercentral.amazon.com/gp/help/1641

It's important that an image is supplied for all products. Upload images by either providing the image URL or use the image upload tool (https://sellercentral.amazon.com/imaging/upload). If using the image upload tool, please submit the template first and then upload images. Until an image is supplied, the SKU will not be buyable. Please note that listing requests for existing ASINs on Amazon do not require submitting an image URL or uploading images.

The Template tab is where you will enter the information for your listings. The default template tab view will show the required, conditionally required, and recommended attributes. Conditionally required attributes become required based on your inputs to the required attributes. Optional attributes are collapsed in each attribute group, and you can expand the optional attributes by clicking the "+" or "-" signs on top of the column. Alternatively, on the top left corner of the sheet, you can select "1" or "2" to collapse or expand all the optional attributes. Option "1" shows the default view which collapses optional attributes and option "2" shows the advanced view which expands all the attributes. The default view will not hide the first attribute in each group. For example, in the screenshot below, the "Style" attribute in the "Discovery" group is optional but not hidden. After selecting the desired Product Type for a row in the template, the required fields in that row will be highlighted in RED, and conditionally required fields and recommended attributes are highlighted in ORANGE. Attributes that are not applicable to your Product Type will be grayed out in that row. We recommend that you provide all the applicable attributes in the default view first, such as highlighted cells, to prevent missing required attribute errors. For the best results, also submit as much optional data as possible for your products. If you are not providing data for a particular non-required field, leave the cell blank. Feel free to add color, boldface, borders and other formatting (not additional text) to the template if it is helpful to you. Note that high ASCII characters (such as ®, ©) and HTML tags are not allowed.

When you have finished entering your product data into the Template tab, you can save the entire workbook as an Excel file or you can save the Template tab (only) as a Text (tab-delimited) (*.txt) file (For the Chinese marketplace, save as Unicode Text (*.txt)): right-click the Template tab, Move or Copy, select 'new book' and 'create a copy', now File, Save As, and choose the correct File Format.
This is your inventory file that you will upload via the Add Products via Upload page in Seller Central.
Upload your file from the "Upload your spreadsheet" section of the Add Products via Upload page in Seller Central, here: https://sellercentral.amazon.com/listing/upload.

When you upload your file, our system will automatically validate your data file as it is submitted. When your submission is complete, you will be able to download a processing report. Any errors in the upload will appear in a Processing Report. This report can be downloaded from the "Spreadsheet upload status" section of the Add Products via Upload page in your seller account on Seller Central, here: https://sellercentral.amazon.com/listing/status.
Note: We recommend first uploading 15 or fewer products for testing purposes. You can upload the rest of your inventory once you have completed a successful test.

From time to time, Amazon will update valid values, data validation rules, explanatory text, and requirements. In the event that you submit an outdated template, we will generate an updated version on your behalf with all of your data prepopulated in it. You will see a link to "Download your submission in the updated template version" on the "Spreadsheet upload status" section of the Add Products via Upload page on Seller Central.
If you have read the Instructions or Data Definitions tabs of this file and still have questions, consult seller Help, starting with this page: https://sellercentral.amazon.com/gp/help/581

values: Every product on Amazon needs one or more product images. Choose images that are clear, straightforward, and easy to understand. They must accurately represent the product and be information-rich and attractively presented. Show only the product that is being offered for sale, with minimal or no propping. Text, logos, and inset images are not allowed. Whenever possible, provide several images, with each one showing different angles and details of the product. This is your opportunity to show your product to your customer, so quality matters.
We reserve the right to reject images that do not meet our image standards.
It is your responsibility to ensure that you have all necessary rights to the images you submit.
*The background for a MAIN image must be pure white (pure white blends in with the Amazon search and item detail pages, which have RGB  values of 255,255,255).

*A MAIN image must not be a graphic or illustration and must not contain accessories that are not being dispatched with the product, props that may confuse the customer, text that is not part of the product, or any logos, watermarks or inset images.
*The product must fill 85% or more of the image.

*MAIN images should be supplemented with additional images showing different sides of a product, the product in use, or details that are not visible in the MAIN image. For media products, this could include the back cover, sample pages, or screenshots. You can add up to eight (8) images.

*A white background is recommended, but not required. Additional images may not include logos or watermarks, and all props or accessories must be presented in a way that will not cause customer confusion.

Images should be 1000 pixels or more in either height or width as this will enable the zoom function on the website (zoom has been proven to enhance sales). Files measuring less than 500 pixels on the longest side will be rejected by our system.
*Amazon accepts JPEG (.jpg), TIFF (.tif), or GIF (.gif) file formats (JPEG files are preferred as they are smaller in size and can therefore be processed and uploaded more quickly).

*A suggested way to name an image file is to save the image on your web server using the product SKU as the file name followed by the view type or variant code--MAIN, PT01-PT08 (additional images), SWCH (usually a color swatch only used on products with more than one variation). Examples: 8845013515.MAIN.jpg, 8845013515.PT01.jpg, 8845013515.SWCH.jpg

You have two options to upload your image files:
(1) Once you have named each image file and saved them to your drive folder, please compress the folder into a zip file. Submit the template without image attributes filled to create the offers on Amazon. Use the Processing Summary to confirm the products are created without errors. Then, proceed to the image upload tool (https://sellercentral.amazon.com/imaging/upload) to upload your images for the listed products. Without providing images, the SKU will not be searchable for customers.
(2) Once you have named the image file and saved it to your web server, enter the URL of the image file in the appropriate cell of your product template.
Please ensure the images you upload comply with Amazon's product image requirements linked here: https://sellercentral.amazon.com/help/hub/reference/G1881
